solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A sweet spice that's not been used

parts.note: pepper is a common spice ground from peppercorns
in mint condition means unused, as new

explanation.surface: A confectionery description: a spicy sweet that has been left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppermints are mint-flavoured confectionery, so one is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Dash of liquor up north

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ale is a malt liquor, a beer

explanation.surface: A splash of spirits being carried up to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of flair and verve is a synonym for style and panache.

clue.text: Lodges in place to drink

parts.note: to place something is to put it
sup means to drink, especially in sips

explanation.surface: Someone lodges in a spot where they can have a drink, like a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Puts up means accommodates as a guest, which is what one who lodges a visitor does.

clue.text: Stretches out and gets pain again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
aches are dull pains, here a verb: has pain

explanation.surface: Someone stretches and then feels sore once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach is to stretch an arm or a distance out to touch something.

clue.text: Multicoloured flag

definitions.meaning: named after the rainbow goddess, and the word suggests a play of many colours
the yellow flag is a species of the plant, so flag is a name for it

explanation.surface: A banner of many colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris means rainbow in Greek, hence many colours, and the flag is a wild iris plant.

clue.text: It has a strong pull in the port trade

definitions.text: It has a strong pull in the port trade

parts.words: It has a strong pull in the port trade
parts.note: reads like an influential figure among dock merchants, but means a vessel that literally tows ships in harbour

explanation.surface: An influential person in the shipping business at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Small powerful harbour vessels tow large ships into and out of port.

clue.text: Eligible to be put in the picture?

definitions.text: Eligible to be put in the picture?

parts.words: Eligible to be put in the picture?
parts.note: put in the picture usually means informed; here it means suited to appear in a photograph

explanation.surface: Someone qualifies to be told what is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks good in photographs is well suited to appear in pictures.

clue.text: Delightful move by footballer in difficult position

parts.note: pretty means attractive or delightful
a pass is a footballer's move sending the ball to a teammate

explanation.surface: A lovely pass by a football player put under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretty pass is an idiom for an awkward or sorry state of affairs.

clue.text: The endless fascination of tea

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: charm is attraction or fascination

explanation.surface: The never-ending appeal of a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha.

clue.text: Too old for love but no longer minding

definitions.meaning: beyond the age for caring about romance
having stopped worrying about anything at all

explanation.surface: An elderly person who has given up on romance and stopped worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Past caring is an idiom for indifference, and read literally it means beyond the time of affection.

clue.text: Get out of order for drumming?

definitions.meaning: an abrupt command telling someone to leave
a command to strike a drum

explanation.surface: A command to leave the room in the middle of a drum lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for go away, and literally an instruction to strike the drum.

clue.text: Go off with food and flowers

parts.note: to pop is to go off with a bang
pies are baked dishes of food

explanation.surface: Someone leaves taking a picnic and a bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppies are red-flowered plants, so the plural names a set of blooms.

clue.text: New place never offers currency

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of the following words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new venue that never takes cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency in the sense of being widespread or current is a synonym for how common a thing is.

clue.text: One shouldn't feel hurt when it's used

definitions.text: One shouldn't feel hurt when it's used

parts.words: One shouldn't feel hurt when it's used
parts.note: sounds like advice on taking criticism, but describes a drug that removes pain

explanation.surface: Advice not to take offence when someone takes advantage of you.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic drug numbs pain, so the patient taking it feels no hurt.

clue.text: Pulls up the grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: draws means pulls, as a cart is drawn

explanation.surface: Someone tears up turf from the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is an expanse of short grass, as on a lawn.

clue.text: Scapegoat that'll get fired in November?

definitions.meaning: a person made to take the blame for others
a guy is the effigy burnt on Bonfire Night, 5 November, in the autumn or fall

explanation.surface: Someone blamed and then sacked late in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: On Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, British people burn an effigy called a guy, and November is in the American fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is an idiom for the person set up to take the blame.

clue.text: Gets on with the passengers

definitions.meaning: to fare is to get on or manage, as in how did you fare
paying passengers in a taxi or bus

explanation.surface: Someone boards the vehicle along with the other travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means to progress or manage, and drivers call paying riders their fares.

clue.text: Wrongful waste of labour

indicators.note: wrongful suggests the letters are put wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that hard work has been unjustly squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat used as a noun means toil or hard work.

clue.text: Prepare to put out with turn of tide

indicators.note: a turn of the following word turns it round so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Getting ready to set sail when the tide turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing is preparing a text for publication, getting it ready to put out.

clue.text: She's arranged similar articles back to back

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, used twice here as the similar pair

indicators.note: back to back means the second copy faces the other way, reversed against the first

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, used twice here as the similar pair

explanation.surface: A woman who has organised matching items in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's name, so it can stand for she.

clue.text: End of gout after unusual cure that may contain salt and pepper

definitions.text: that may contain salt and pepper

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the anagram
unusual signals the letters of the next word are set in an odd order
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A patient trying an odd remedy for gout at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a medical remedy for gout, but 'cure' is only fodder and gout only supplies its last letter; the definition describes a condiment set on a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet is a small container or stand for condiments at table.

clue.text: Move stealthily as an Indian, on young animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
a pup is the young of a dog, seal and others

explanation.surface: An image of someone stalking quietly like a scout, riding a puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep up is to approach slowly and silently without being noticed.

clue.text: Cause of on-going strikes by potters?

definitions.text: Cause of on-going strikes by potters?

parts.words: Cause of on-going strikes by potters?
parts.note: reads like a pottery workers' industrial dispute, but potters are snooker or billiards players whose shots make the ball run on

explanation.surface: Why the pottery workers keep walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker to pot a ball is to sink it, so potters are players, and strikes are shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward spin on a ball makes it keep travelling on after it hits another.

clue.text: Difficult week in a hospital department

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the following words

parts.note: a ward is a room or department in a hospital

explanation.surface: A tough seven days spent on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with, a synonym for troublesome.

clue.text: Crusoe's strange origins

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the name are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: The unusual background of the castaway Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sources are the places something starts from, its origins.

clue.text: Some take him for a scallywag — rightly!

definitions.text: Some take him for a scallywag — rightly!

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, the letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: People regard a man as a rogue, and they are right to.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue, the same as a scallywag.

clue.text: Squirming eel can get entangled

definitions.note: the verb phrase stands for the verb, to wind or tangle together

indicators.note: squirming means wriggling, so the letters of the words wriggle into new places

explanation.surface: A wriggling eel caught in a tin becomes tangled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlace is to entwine or wrap around, a formal synonym for entangle.

clue.text: Man-of-war?

parts.note: a man-of-war is usually a warship, but here a man of the South African war

explanation.surface: A question about a sailing warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Boer settlers fought the British in the Boer Wars of South Africa.

clue.text: Breathing space

parts.note: normally a pause or respite, read literally as the organ where breathing happens

explanation.surface: A short rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of respiration is literally a space where air is breathed in.

clue.text: Possible customer goes to America for brochure

parts.note: a prospect is a potential client
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A potential buyer travels to the States in search of a sales leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a printed document advertising a school, company or offer.

clue.text: Musical character to have on the staff

definitions.text: Musical character to have on the staff

parts.words: Musical character to have on the staff
parts.note: sounds like a theatrical person employed by a company, but staff is the five-line stave

explanation.surface: An employer wants a performer on the payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of the stave fixing the pitch of notes.

clue.text: Those who believe in it should have their heads examined

definitions.text: Those who believe in it should have their heads examined

parts.words: Those who believe in it should have their heads examined
parts.note: the idiom for being foolish is read literally, as the skull-reading practice demands

explanation.surface: A jibe that believers in something are mad.
explanation.definitionFit: This discredited pseudoscience claimed to read character from the bumps on the skull.
